besluite.fout: The second verb 'dek' has no subject of its own, so on a first reading it can attach to 'dit' (the dough) instead of to Ouma.
besluite.rede: Giving 'dek' its own subject 'sy' makes clear that Ouma covers the bowl, without changing what happens, and the comma before 'en' is the AWS comma between two full clauses.

besluite.fout: 'Druk' stands without an object, so the reader has to work out what Ouma is pressing.
besluite.rede: Naming the dough already in her bowl fixes the vague verb and adds no new fact, since that is what she is pressing.

besluite.fout: 'Die onderkant van sy hand' is vague: it could mean the whole palm or the lower part of the hand.
besluite.rede: The vagueness is real, but 'die onderkant van sy handpalm' settles which part of the hand is used to knead, and that is a content decision for the writer, not a language one.

besluite.fout: 'Dus' reads like a formal conclusion in an argument, which is stiff in a Grade 5 story.
besluite.rede: 'Daarom' is the natural spoken word for the same cause and effect, with the same word order and the same meaning.
